correctness.rationale: An arbitrary complement of a super dominating set has at most two vertices: a private neighbor witnessing one omitted vertex must see none of the others; in a multipartite graph this forces all other omissions into its own part, contradicting witnesses for those omissions when there are two or more. For two omissions the two relevant parts must both be non-singletons. Partition partners are therefore controlled exactly by residual singleton or Q-edge blocks. Exhaustive cases k=2,3,4 yield the coefficients, while k>=5 cannot leave a complement of at most two vertices. Independently programmed direct neighborhood/partition checks verify 38 profiles at orders 7--9, plus two boundary/example checks; finite checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: The general existence/maximum study of super-coalition partitions motivates cardinality refinement. This theorem supplies every coefficient for an unbounded natural graph class, identifies the exact threshold for four coalition classes, and gives direct formulas from part sizes. Its matching/triangle structure is a substantive interaction among blocks, not merely a relabelled domination-set count or a small numerical increment.
